# Setup
```{r install/load packages}
list.of.packages <-
  c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "vegan", "rstatix")
new.packages <-
  list.of.packages[!(list.of.packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new.packages)) install.packages(new.packages)


library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(vegan)
```

```{r data download and minor fixes}
data1<-read.csv("NBWQ_Combined_RAW_Data20220224.csv")
data1[data1 ==""]<- NA
data1

tide1<-read.csv("NOAA-MLLW_Tides_minute_2021-22.csv")

chlA<- read.csv("ZP_ChlorophyllData_TIDY_02-02-2022.csv")

data1
tide1
chlA
```

```{r join date & time}
#For sake of simplicity, we will substitute the HOBOtime into the Blank spaces of SampleTime_Water
data1<-data1 %>% 
  mutate(SampleTime_Water = ifelse(is.na(data1$SampleTime_Water), data1$HOBOtime, data1$SampleTime_Water)) %>% 
  unite(col = "DateTime", Day, SampleTime_Water, sep = " ", remove = "FALSE")
  

tide1<-tide1 %>% 
  unite(col = "DateTime", date, time, sep = " ", remove = "FALSE")
  
```

```{r Fix DateTime For tides and survey data}
data2 <- data1 %>%  mutate(DateTime = format(strptime(DateTime, "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M"))) %>% 
  mutate(DateTime = as.POSIXct(DateTime))
tide2 <- tide1 %>%  mutate(DateTime = format(strptime(DateTime, "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M"))) %>% 
  mutate(DateTime = as.POSIXct(DateTime))
```

```{r tranform date field}
#date field must be transformed into factor and told what specific order it should have for later graphs
data2$Date <- factor(data2$Date, levels = c("12/4/2021", "12/15/2021", "1/8/2022", "1/16/2022", "1/23/2022"))
```


```{r create new TideChange column}
tide2 <- tide2 %>% mutate(TideChange = (pred-lag(pred)))
#found and removed 4 outliers for TideChange resulting from disjunction in tides across sampling dates
##  to test for outliers of this type, turn off code below code run unique(tide2$TideChange) and select (number of sample dates)-1 most extreme values
tide2$TideChange[abs(tide2$TideChange) >= 0.1] <- NA
```



```{r fix object classes}
data2$Site <- as.factor(data2$Site)
data2$Bed_Stability <- as.factor(data2$Bed_Stability)
data2$CurrentDirection <- as.factor(data2$CurrentDirection)
data2$PPFD <- as.numeric(data2$PPFD)
view(data2)
```

```{r Make selections for what will be included in joined data frames}
data2<- data2 %>% select(c("Site", "Bed_Stability", "Date", "DateTime", "Turbidity_NTU","Sample_ID",  "CurrentDirection", "Temp_C", "DO_mg.L", "DO_.", "Depth_PAR", "PPFD", "BottomDepth_ft", "VegDepth_ft",  "ForelUleColorCategory", "HOBOtime_start"))

tide2<- tide2 %>% select(c("DateTime", "pred", "TideChange"))

chlA2<- chlA %>% select(c("Sample_ID", "F.Value", "X.ug.L.", "Dilution.", "CalculatedConcentration.ug.L.", "CorrectedConcentration.ug.L."))

```

```{r Join 1}
fieldXchlA_join<- data2 %>% left_join(chlA2, by = "Sample_ID")
fieldXchlA_join$Sample_ID <- as.factor(fieldXchlA_join$Sample_ID)
```


```{r Join 2}
data_join<- fieldXchlA_join %>% left_join(tide2, by = "DateTime")
save(data_join, file = "NBWQdata_Tides.Rdata")
```

#Questions
##Question Summary
DANA
1.  Is there an association between light availability and eelgrass bed stability? (ANOVA)

2. Is temperature and chlorophyll significantly different between stable and ephemeral sites?(multivariate logistic regression)

3.  How do chlorophyll levels impact light availability in the lower bay?

*BONUS QUESTION: What other factors correlate with high/increased chlorophyll?

MATTHEW
4.	How do differences between daily high and low tides impact data

5.	Are more extreme high and low tides associated with lower quantities of light scattering materials in the water column

6.	Are lower average daily tidal ranges associated with higher levels of light scattering materials in the water column 

BONUS: Correlation between temperature, salinity, and their impact on DO. Test for good data.

BONUS: Forel-Ule color test comparing color trends between sites

BONUS: Does increased distance from the harbor mouth negatively impact water quality factors [DO, turbidity, color, light availability PAR,]?


Dependent		     Independent	       Test				     Purpose/description

Turbidity		    ←	Depth	        	Regression	        	Observe if depth may correlate with some other variable ↑ NTU such as current		
Color           ←	tide/depth    	ANOVA(2way???)	    	Indiv assessment of depth impact on color
Chlorophyll     ←	Temperature	    Regression	        	Indiv assessment of Temp impact on chlorophyll
Turbidity		    ←	|tide change|   Regression	        	Indiv assessment of tide change impact on NTU
Light		        ←	Chlorophyll   	Regression		        Indiv assessment of chlorophyll impact on light
Turbidity	    	←	Temp	        	Multiple Regression		Observe impact of environmental variables on turbidity

# stepwise multiple logistic regression (book chapter)
```{r}
# model1 to include depth along with ppfd and date, model2 no depth

model1 <- glm(Stable ~ PPFD + Depth_PAR + Date, data = data_join, family = binomial)
model1
model2 <- glm(Stable ~ PPFD+ Date, data = data_join, family = binomial)
model2
model3 <- glm(Stable ~ PPFD+ Date+ Turbidity_NTU, data = data_join, family = binomial)
model4 <- glm(Stable ~ PPFD+ Date+ CorrectedConcentration_ug.L, data = data_join, family = binomial)
#aic measures fit of model, lower score indicates better fit. Depth did not impact
AIC(model1, model2, model3, model4)
AIC(model1, model2, model4)
```

##multiplot function
This is the definition of multiplot. It can take any number of plot objects as arguments, or if it can take a list of plot objects passed to plotlist.
```{r Multiple Plot Funciton: multiplot}
# ggplot objects can be passed in ..., or to plotlist (as a list of ggplot objects)
# - cols:   Number of columns in layout
# - layout: A matrix specifying the layout. If present, 'cols' is ignored.
#
# If the layout is something like matrix(c(1,2,3,3), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE),
# then plot 1 will go in the upper left, 2 will go in the upper right, and
# 3 will go all the way across the bottom.
#
multiplot <- function(..., plotlist=NULL, file, cols=1, layout=NULL) {
  library(grid)

  # Make a list from the ... arguments and plotlist
  plots <- c(list(...), plotlist)

  numPlots = length(plots)

  # If layout is NULL, then use 'cols' to determine layout
  if (is.null(layout)) {
    # Make the panel
    # ncol: Number of columns of plots
    # nrow: Number of rows needed, calculated from # of cols
    layout <- matrix(seq(1, cols * ceiling(numPlots/cols)),
                    ncol = cols, nrow = ceiling(numPlots/cols))
  }

 if (numPlots==1) {
    print(plots[[1]])

  } else {
    # Set up the page
    grid.newpage()
    pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(nrow(layout), ncol(layout))))

    # Make each plot, in the correct location
    for (i in 1:numPlots) {
      # Get the i,j matrix positions of the regions that contain this subplot
      matchidx <- as.data.frame(which(layout == i, arr.ind = TRUE))

      print(plots[[i]], vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = matchidx$row,
                                      layout.pos.col = matchidx$col))
    }
  }
}
```

```{r plot mean_PPFD}
  theme(legend.position="none", axis.title.x = element_text(size = 40), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 30), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 40), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 30))+
  coord_cartesian(ylim=(c(45,1000)))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1000, 250))+
  theme(text = element_text(size = 20))
MPPFD
```

```{r plot median FU color-category}

  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (median_color - se_color), ymax = (median_color + se_color)), width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.9))+

MFU
```

